title: E-commerce Footwear: A Three-Month Technical Turnaround
excerpt: Site health to 85%, PageSpeed 92, and search growth concentrated after mid-month fixes for a footwear retailer. Read the case.
rm_title: Ecommerce SEO for Footwear: Site Turnaround
rm_desc: Ecommerce SEO for footwear: site health to 85%, PageSpeed to 92 for a retailer. Read the case.
content: This ecommerce SEO for footwear case covers a premium retailer whose search presence was almost entirely branded: people who already knew the name could find it, and nobody else could. Underneath sat an unhealthy site and a backlink profile leaning on low-authority, largely nofollow links.
What ecommerce SEO for footwear looked like here

The turnaround was technical first: caching, minification and page-speed remediation, XML and HTML sitemaps generated and submitted, and schema markup implemented across product and collection templates. The backlink profile was audited for anchor relevance with a disavow filed for harmful links, on-page work covered titles, meta descriptions and heading structure, and landing-page analysis separated high-impression pages from the ones that convert.
Why branded-only visibility is a warning sign

A retailer that only ranks for its own name is invisible to the much larger pool of shoppers who do not know the brand yet and are searching by category or product type instead. Ecommerce SEO for footwear specifically means competing on terms like shoe types, use cases and style descriptors, beyond the brand name, since that is where new customer discovery actually happens rather than where existing customers confirm they have found the right site.

Site health improved to 85%, PageSpeed scored 92, and on-page evaluation reached an A− grade. November closed at 220 clicks from 9,240 impressions at a 2.4% CTR, with the growth concentrated in the second half of the month, immediately following the optimisation work. Mid-tier non-branded keywords settled at positions 10–11, the band where CTR work pays next.

Three months fixes a site and starts a trend; proving a compounding one takes longer. The honest description is a foundation laid, with momentum visible at the point of reporting. The absolute numbers are modest by design, this was a niche retailer, not a mass-market store, and the biggest constraint identified, backlink authority, was still outstanding when the reporting period closed. We said so in the report on this ecommerce SEO for footwear engagement, rather than waiting for a stakeholder to ask why the number was not bigger.
Why the technical fixes came before content

Google's own page experience documentation treats site health and speed as a gating factor before content quality gets fully credited, a slow, unhealthy site suppresses the ranking potential of even excellent product copy sitting on it. Ecommerce SEO for footwear on a technically unhealthy platform would have wasted content investment on pages the crawler was already deprioritising, which is why the sequencing here started with caching and site health rather than product copy.

This engagement ran through our SEO & GEO / AIO / AEO service, alongside the schema and structured-data work covered in our analytics page. Retailers with a similar branded-only visibility problem can use either page to scope an ecommerce SEO for footwear diagnostic, or an equivalent one for their own category.

A backlink profile leaning on low-authority, largely nofollow links fails to help and, in some cases, actively signals low quality to search engines if the pattern looks manipulative rather than organic. Filing a disavow for the harmful links removed that drag before the technical and content work had to compete against it, rather than trying to out-optimise a backlink profile that was actively working against the site the entire time.
Client described by sector rather than named, and every figure is reported exactly as recorded at the time.
